title: Derived-section presentation by bounded-below hypersheaves
statement:
A small Grothendieck site is a small category with specified covering sieves, containing the maximal sieve and closed under pullback of sieves and transitivity; a sieve is a collection of arrows with fixed target closed under precomposition. A family covers when its generated sieve covers. No fibre products in the underlying category are required. All sizes use [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $\mathbf D(\Lambda)$ be the enhanced localization of cochain complexes of $\Lambda$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms, retaining derived mapping complexes and all higher composition data [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A $\mathbf D(\Lambda)$-valued hypersheaf is a coherent presheaf $F$ [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] such that for every hypercover $T_\bullet\to T$ the map $F(T)\to\operatorname{holim}_{[n]\in\Delta}F(T_n)$ is an equivalence. Here a hypercover is an augmented simplicial family of representable presheaves whose maps to all matching presheaves are locally surjective after sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]; $F$ on a family is the product of its values. Write $\operatorname{Hyp}_{\ge a}(\mathcal C,\Lambda)$ for the full enhanced category of such $F$ with $H^i(F(T))=0$ for every $T$ and $i<a$, for a fixed integer $a$. Morphisms are coherent natural transformations, and mapping complexes are the derived ends in the coherent presheaf category.

For any such site $\mathcal C$, let $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C,\Lambda)$ be the category of sheaves of modules over the constant sheaf of rings $\Lambda$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Write $\mathbf D_{\ge a}(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C,\Lambda))$ for the full enhanced localization of their complexes whose cohomology sheaves vanish in degrees below $a$. Here $R\Gamma(T,-)$ denotes the right derived functor of evaluation $N\mapsto N(T)$ from module sheaves to $\Lambda$-modules. Derived evaluation defines an equivalence, including derived mapping complexes,
$$M\longmapsto (T\longmapsto R\Gamma(T,M)),\qquad
\mathbf D_{\ge a}(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C,\Lambda))\simeq\operatorname{Hyp}_{\ge a}(\mathcal C,\Lambda).$$
For the inverse image $M$ of $F$, the cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^i(M)$ is the sheafification of $T\mapsto H^i(F(T))$. These equivalences are compatible with changing $a$ and with localization to a slice site: on $\mathcal C/T$, the presheaf for the restricted object has value $R\Gamma(S,M)$ at $(S\to T)$. In particular the compatibility is specified as enhanced natural equivalences, not only isomorphisms of degree-zero morphism groups.

source.place: Tag 0DA2, lemma-hypercovering-equivalence-bounded-modules, is the ordinary total-hypercover descent prototype only. The enhanced derived-section presentation on arbitrary Grothendieck sites is an agent-formulated foundation. Hemo--Richarz--Scholbach, Constructible sheaves on schemes, section 3, printed p.6, discusses the analogous hypercomplete-module model on the pro-etale site and cites SAG Theorem 2.1.2.2. WANTED: an archived enhanced bounded-below derived-section/hypersheaf comparison for arbitrary sites.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C,\Lambda)$ and $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}_\Lambda)$. Use the exact module-sheafification theorem for arbitrary covering-sieve topologies, applied to the constant presheaf ring and its associated ring sheaf $\underline\Lambda$. It gives an exact left adjoint $b:\mathcal P\to\mathcal A$ to the underlying-$\Lambda$-presheaf functor $i$, identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of $bP$ with ordinary sheafification, and gives $bi\cong\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}$. It also identifies $i$ with an equivalence from $\mathcal A$ onto the category $\mathcal S$ of sheaves valued in ordinary $\Lambda$-modules: the unit is an isomorphism on every sheaf-valued presheaf and the compatible associated-ring action is unique. The small-sieve-site Grothendieck theorem applies to $\mathcal S$, hence to $\mathcal A$ through this equivalence: transport its colimits and generator, and use that the equivalence preserves kernels and cokernels to transport filtered exactness. The enough-injectives theorem therefore applies to $\mathcal A$. All sizes are the chosen ones; no representable is assumed to be a sheaf and no pullback object in $\mathcal C$ is used.

source.place: Agent-written abelian setup; section 5 opening supplies the fixed-coefficient sheafification adjunction. Exactness and injectives are taken from the cited existing nodes, rather than assumed from a definition.

proof.text: Use the projective model on $\operatorname{Ch}(\Lambda)$ and apply the Quillen-section rectification theorem to the constant diagram indexed by $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$, with identity transition functors. Strict sections are precisely complexes in $\mathcal P$, and weak equivalences are precisely objectwise quasi-isomorphisms. It identifies $\mathbf D(\mathcal P)$ with coherent $\mathbf D(\Lambda)$-valued presheaves, over evaluations, including the stated coherent-end mapping complexes and their composition. In particular a hypersheaf $F$ has a strict presheaf-complex representative $P$, unique up to equivalence in this enhanced category. The hypothesis on its lower bound says exactly that the presheaves $H^r(P)$ are zero for $r<a$. Exactness of $b$ therefore gives $H^r(bP)=bH^r(P)=0$ for $r<a$.

source.place: Agent-written application of existing enriched diagram rectification; source section 3 supplies the objectwise presheaf-complex model. This step does not assert hyperdescent.

proof.text:
For $M\in\mathbf D_{\ge a}(\mathcal A)$ choose an injective complex $I$ representing $M$ with $I^r=0$ for $r<a$, using the bounded-below injective-representative theorem. Since $b$ is exact and $b\dashv i$, $i$ sends injective sheaves to injective objects of $\mathcal P$. Both $I$ and $iI$ are K-injective by the bounded-below injective criterion. Hence their ordinary Hom complexes compute the derived Hom complexes: for a quasi-isomorphism $s$, its cone is acyclic, and applying $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(-,I)$ (respectively $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(-,iI)$) makes $s$ a quasi-isomorphism. More explicitly, the enriched localization comparison on these Hom complexes induces on $H^n$ the cited K-injective Hom-localization bijection applied to $P[-n]$, so the comparison is a quasi-isomorphism in every degree. Every bounded-below derived object has an injective representative, and the same cited lemma says that a quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives is a homotopy equivalence. Thus the full dg category of bounded-below injectives presents the enhanced bounded-below localization, including composition. Degreewise sheafification adjunction now gives the chain-complex adjunction
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(P,iI)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}^\bullet(P,iI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}^\bullet(bP,I)=R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(bP,M).$$
The signs agree because $b$ is additive and is applied degreewise. In particular for two bounded-below injective representatives $I,J$ one has $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}^\bullet(iI,iJ)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}^\bullet(I,J)$, compatibly with composition. Thus $M\mapsto iI$ is an enhanced fully faithful functor $J$; the displayed adjunction and enriched Yoneda give its enhanced unit, not merely a family of homotopy-category maps. Evaluation of $iI$ at $T$ is $I(T)$, the K-injective computation of $R\Gamma(T,M)$; it is zero in complex degrees below $a$.

source.place: Agent-written mapping-complex argument using exact sheafification, bounded-below injectives, and enriched localization; this supplies the enhancement rather than inferring it from ordinary derived functors.

proof.text: The presheaf $iI$ satisfies hyperdescent. Indeed let $f:P\to Q$ be any local quasi-isomorphism in $\mathcal P$. Since $b$ is exact, $b\operatorname{Cone}(f)=\operatorname{Cone}(bf)$ is acyclic: its cohomology is the sheafification of the cohomology presheaf of $\operatorname{Cone}(f)$. The adjunction of step 3 identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}^\bullet(\operatorname{Cone}(f),iI)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}^\bullet(b\operatorname{Cone}(f),I)$, which is acyclic by K-injectivity. Thus $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(f,iI)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply the local-orthogonality characterization to obtain the asserted equivalence $I(T)\simeq\operatorname{holim}_n I(U_n)$ for every hypercover. This proves that $J$ lands in $\operatorname{Hyp}_{\ge a}$ without any subcanonical, fibre-product, point, or cohomological-dimension hypothesis on the site.

source.place: Theorem 5.7 and Lemma 5.10 in local-orthogonality form, applied after the explicit sheafification/Hom computation. This replaces the unsupported matching-limit and spectral-sequence assertions.

proof.text: Conversely let $F$ be a hypersheaf with lower bound $a$ and represent it by $P$ as in step 2. Take $M=bP$ and its bounded-below injective representative $I$ from step 3. Choose the derived isomorphism $bP\simeq I$. Since $I$ is K-injective, the K-injective Hom-localization bijection represents it by a chain map $v:bP\to I$. Its cohomology maps are those of the derived isomorphism, so $v$ is a quasi-isomorphism, even if the chosen complex $bP$ itself has nonzero terms below $a$. The derived unit $u:P\to J(bP)=iI$ is represented by the sheafification unit followed by $iv$. Its sheafification is the quasi-isomorphism $bP\to I$, so $u$ is a local quasi-isomorphism. Both its source and its target are hypersheaves, the target by step 4. Apply local orthogonality with targets $P$ and $iI$. Surjectivity of $H^0R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(u,P)$ gives $r:iI\to P$ with $ru=\mathrm{id}_P$. Injectivity of $H^0R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(u,iI)$ and the equation $(ur)u=u=\mathrm{id}_{iI}u$ give $ur=\mathrm{id}_{iI}$. Thus $u$ is an equivalence in the objectwise presheaf derived category, hence under rectification is an enhanced presheaf equivalence $F\simeq J(M)$. Together with step 3 this proves full faithfulness and essential surjectivity; the unit and the identity $biI=I$ supply enhanced quasi-inverse comparisons. No Postnikov extensions have to be chosen or glued.

source.place: Agent-written reconstruction from sheafification, using the source local-equivalence criterion. The two inverse equations are written explicitly; they are not a new lemma.

proof.text: Exactness of $b$ gives $\mathcal H^r(M)=\mathcal H^r(bP)=b(T\mapsto H^r(P(T)))$. Rectification identifies $H^r(P(T))$ with $H^r(F(T))$, so this is precisely the claimed sheafification of the cohomology presheaf. The same $b$, the same derived-section functor $J$, and the same enhanced adjunction are used for every $a$. Their units and counits restrict to each full subcategory with the stated bound; thus the equivalences commute coherently with the inclusions as $a$ changes, including their mapping complexes.

source.place: Agent-written cohomology and change-of-bound verification from exactness and the already constructed enhanced adjunction.

proof.text: Apply slice sheafification compatibility first to the constant ring presheaf. The unit-compatible comparison identifies $\underline\Lambda|_T$ with the constant ring sheaf on $\mathcal C/T$, as a ring and naturally in constant scalars. The same comparison for $\Lambda$-module presheaves shows that restriction is exact: kernels of sheaves are computed sectionwise, and a cokernel is sheafification of the sectionwise cokernel; restricting this construction gives the slice cokernel by the cited natural comparison. The unique associated-ring module actions of step 1 make these also the kernels and cokernels of ringed module sheaves. The existing arbitrary-topology extension-adjoint theorem supplies an exact left adjoint to module restriction $j_T^*$; its hypothesis of preserving zero morphisms holds because restriction is sectionwise. The right-adjoint injective criterion therefore shows that $j_T^*$ sends injectives to injectives. Thus $j_T^*I$ is a bounded-below injective representative of the exactly restricted object $j_T^*M$. At $(S\to T)$ its complex of sections is literally $I(S)$, so both $J(M)|_{\mathcal C/T}$ and $J_{\mathcal C/T}(j_T^*M)$ are computed by this same complex with the same restriction chain maps. The identity holds on the induced Hom complexes and under iterated slice restrictions. On these dg models it is an identity of functors and composition maps; enriched localization gives the specified coherent natural equivalences for arbitrary $M$, compatible with changing $a$. The same equality of complexes preserves the bound on the slice.

source.place: Agent-written slice comparison using Modules on Sites exact slice extension/restriction, as carried by the cited node; equality is checked before localization.

proof_origin.place: Agent-written exact-sheafification and bounded-below injective argument, using Choudhury--Gallauer Theorem 5.7 only for the independently isolated local-hyperdescent characterization. The current main-20261015 compactification proof opening motivates this foundation; it does not contain the enhanced comparison proof.
